config.title: prefers-reduced-motion

intro.title: prefers-reduced-motion
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage with a spinning animation and learn how to respect user preferences for reduced motion. You will use the CSS `prefers-reduced-motion` media query to detect if a user has requested less animation on their device. The core concept is applying conditional styles based on system settings, using keyframes for animation and media queries for control. This involves writing CSS rules that toggle or modify animations when `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is active. By the end, you'll create a page that spins an element smoothly by default but stops or slows the spin for users who prefer reduced motion.
intro.usecase: The `prefers-reduced-motion` media query is essential for building accessible web applications that respect user preferences. In real-world products like admin dashboards with animated charts, e-commerce sites with carousels, or news apps with auto-scrolling feeds, developers use it to disable or simplify animations for users who experience motion sickness or vestibular disorders. This ensures compliance with accessibility standards (WCAG) and improves the user experience for a significant portion of the audience. Implementing it involves conditionally applying CSS rules to reduce or remove motion-based effects while maintaining core functionality.

objectives: Apply the prefers-reduced-motion media query to CSS animations
Configure alternative styles for users who prefer reduced motion
Construct CSS transitions that respect user motion preferences
Implement fallback animations using the no-preference condition
Manipulate animation properties based on user accessibility settings
Integrate motion detection with existing CSS animation code
Control animation behavior through media query conditions

steps.title: Understand the prefers-reduced-motion media query
steps.instruction: Create a CSS file and add a comment explaining what prefers-reduced-motion does.
steps.hint: Start with a comment that describes the purpose of this media query for accessibility.
steps.analogousExample: /* This media query checks if the user prefers reduced motion */
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS file with a descriptive comment about prefers-reduced-motion.
successCriteria: The comment explains that prefers-reduced-motion detects user preference for reduced motion.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your comment clearly explains what prefers-reduced-motion does.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. Start with a comment that describes the purpose of the prefers-reduced-motion media query.

steps.title: Create a basic animation without accessibility considerations
steps.instruction: Define a CSS keyframes animation named 'slide' that moves an element from left: 0 to left: 100px.
steps.hint: Use @keyframes to create an animation. The animation should have at least two keyframes (like 'from' and 'to' or percentages) to define the movement.
steps.seedCode:
/* Add your comment here */

/* Define your keyframes animation named 'slide' below */
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a keyframes animation defined that moves an element horizontally.
successCriteria: A @keyframes rule named 'slide' is defined with at least two keyframes that change the left property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your animation is named 'slide' and uses the left property to create horizontal movement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The keyframes animation isn't defined correctly. Remember to use @keyframes followed by a name, and define the movement using the left property.

steps.title: Add the animation to an HTML element
steps.instruction: Create a CSS rule for a div element with the class 'animated-box' that applies your 'slide' animation. Set the animation-name to 'slide' and animation-duration to 2 seconds.
steps.hint: Use the class selector .animated-box followed by curly braces. Inside, add animation-name: slide; and animation-duration: 2s;
steps.expectedOutcome: The 'slide' animation will be applied to any element with class 'animated-box', making it animate for 2 seconds.
successCriteria: A CSS rule for .animated-box exists with animation-name: slide; and animation-duration: 2s;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you have both animation-name and animation-duration properties in your .animated-box rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule for .animated-box is missing or incomplete. Check that you have animation-name: slide; and animation-duration: 2s;

steps.title: Introduce the prefers-reduced-motion media query syntax
steps.instruction: Add a media query for prefers-reduced-motion that targets the animated-box class and sets animation to none when motion is reduced.
steps.hint: Use @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { } and inside, write .animated-box { animation: none; }
steps.expectedOutcome: The CSS file now includes a media query that disables the animation when the user prefers reduced motion.
successCriteria: The code contains @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) with a rule for .animated-box setting animation to none.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have the exact syntax: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .animated-box { animation: none; } }
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. Review the syntax for the prefers-reduced-motion media query and ensure it targets the .animated-box class.

steps.title: Create a reduced motion alternative
steps.instruction: Inside the existing prefers-reduced-motion media query, add a CSS rule for the .animated-box class that sets animation to 'none' to disable the animation when reduced motion is preferred.
steps.hint: The media query is already set up. You just need to add a selector for .animated-box inside it and set the animation property to 'none'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The media query now contains a rule that disables the animation for .animated-box when users prefer reduced motion.
successCriteria: The .animated-box selector is inside the prefers-reduced-motion media query with animation: none;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the .animated-box selector inside the media query with animation: none;
steps.feedbackWrong: The media query should contain a rule for .animated-box that sets animation to 'none'.

steps.title: Apply the reduced motion styles to the animated element
steps.instruction: Inside the prefers-reduced-motion media query, target the .animated-box class and set its animation property to 'none'.
steps.hint: Add a CSS rule for .animated-box inside the existing media query block.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .animated-box element will have its animation disabled when the user's system prefers reduced motion.
successCriteria: The .animated-box rule is correctly placed inside the media query with animation: none.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the .animated-box rule is inside the media query and sets animation to none.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added a rule for .animated-box inside the media query with animation: none.

steps.title: Test the animation with and without reduced motion preference
steps.instruction: Open your browser's developer tools and find the 'Toggle device toolbar' or 'Responsive design mode' option to simulate reduced motion preferences.
steps.hint: Look for a 'Rendering' tab in developer tools or search for 'prefers-reduced-motion' in the settings to enable simulation.
steps.analogousExample:
/* In browser dev tools: 
1. Open Elements/Inspector tab
2. Find 'Toggle device toolbar' (Ctrl+Shift+M)
3. Click 'More options' → 'Add device type'
4. Enable 'prefers-reduced-motion' simulation */
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll be able to toggle between normal and reduced motion modes to see the animation stop when reduced motion is enabled.
successCriteria: Learner has opened browser developer tools and located the reduced motion simulation option.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're in the 'Rendering' or 'Accessibility' section of developer tools to find the motion preference toggle.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try opening developer tools (F12 or right-click → Inspect) and looking for 'Toggle device toolbar' or 'Emulate CSS media feature prefers-reduced-motion'.

steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS class .transition-box is created with basic styling and a transition property.
successCriteria: The .transition-box class is defined with properties like width, height, background-color, and transition.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the .transition-box class, but make sure it includes properties like width, height, background-color, and transition.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .transition-box class is not defined correctly. Check the instruction and try again.

steps.title: Add the transition example to the HTML
steps.instruction: Add a new HTML element with the class 'transition-box' to your HTML file.
steps.hint: Create a <div> element and give it the class name 'transition-box'.
steps.expectedOutcome: An HTML element with the class 'transition-box' is added to the HTML file.
successCriteria: The HTML file contains a <div> element with class="transition-box".
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an HTML element, but make sure it has the exact class name 'transition-box'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Please add an HTML element with the class 'transition-box' to your HTML file.

steps.title: Review and consolidate the implementation
steps.instruction: Add the missing CSS rule for the 'transition-box' class with a hover effect and its reduced-motion alternative.
steps.hint: Define a CSS class that changes smoothly on hover, then add a media query to disable the transition when reduced motion is preferred.
steps.expectedOutcome: The CSS file will have a complete 'transition-box' class with a hover transition and a reduced-motion alternative, alongside the existing animation example.
successCriteria: The 'transition-box' class is defined with a transition property and a hover effect, and a media query for reduced motion disables the transition.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the 'transition-box' class has a transition property and a hover effect, and that the reduced-motion media query disables the transition.
steps.feedbackWrong: The 'transition-box' class or its reduced-motion alternative is missing or incorrect. Review the example and try again.
